answer: Make identity expensive to copy but cheap to keep: each agent locks a modest refundable stake and earns trust only from completed work that independent peers verify over time, like an ember that must be tended, not duplicated. New identities start with no voting or reward rights until they build a checkable history. A grove of long-lived peers cross-checks overlapping work, so fresh clones cannot vouch for each other. Running an island of fakes means funding every stake and waiting out every probation, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its standing.
